McKenzie County is located in western North Dakota, with Watford City serving as the county seat. The area is known for wide open land, agriculture, and energy production. Each year, the county conducts tax deed sales for properties acquired through the tax foreclosure process. This article explains how McKenzie County tax sales work, when they are held, and what investors should expect. It also walks through bidding rules, payment terms, due diligence steps, and where to find official updates.

What is McKenzie County tax deed investing

McKenzie County does not sell traditional tax lien certificates to private investors. Instead, it sells tax foreclosure properties through a public tax deed auction. These properties became county owned after unpaid property taxes went through the statutory foreclosure process under North Dakota law. Investors bid on the property itself, not an interest rate. The winning bidder pays the purchase price in full at the sale and later receives a county deed once paperwork is completed.

Important Details

Key Takeaways

  • McKenzie County conducts tax deed sales for properties acquired through tax foreclosure, with auctions held on the third Tuesday of November.
  • Investors bid on properties directly, not interest rates, and must pay in full at the auction.
  • Due diligence is crucial; buyers must verify property details before bidding to avoid potential issues.
  • The county offers a variety of rural properties, making it appealing for tax deed investors seeking high returns.
  • Investors can contact the McKenzie County Auditor and Treasurer office for procedure details and updates.

Fun Facts About the County

  • McKenzie County is the largest county in North Dakota by land area.
  • Watford City is a major service center for western North Dakota.
  • Parts of Theodore Roosevelt National Park are located in the county.
  • The local economy is supported by energy production, farming, and tourism.

Attractions and Economic Highlights

  • Attractions include Theodore Roosevelt National Park North Unit.
  • Transportation routes include US Highway 85 and North Dakota Highway 23.
  • Main industries include oil and gas, agriculture, and tourism.
  • Outdoor recreation includes hiking, wildlife viewing, and scenic drives.

Why McKenzie County is ideal for tax deed investors

  • Buyers can target high returns by purchasing below local market values.
  • Rural properties can offer a lower risk investment when researched carefully.
  • Many parcels are vacant land, which can reduce occupancy issues.
  • Minimum bid prices are published, helping investors plan bids.
  • North Dakota tax deed sales allow investors to focus on asset value rather than interest bidding.

Auction Process for McKenzie County tax deed sales

McKenzie County holds its annual tax deed auction at the McKenzie County Courthouse Board Room. The sale is typically scheduled for the third Tuesday of November at 10:00 AM Central Time. Property lists are usually published after the first week of October. Investors should review the list early and conduct research before sale day.

How the auction works

  1. Analyze property details

    Review the official property list when it is released.

  2. Complete registration

    Arrive early on auction day to register.

  3. Verify tax status

    Sign the Delinquent Tax Oath confirming all North Dakota property taxes are paid.

  4. Monitor opening bids

    Each parcel opens at the county’s posted minimum sale price.

  5. Place your bids

    Bidding continues until the highest bid is reached.

  6. Complete immediate payment

    The winning bidder pays immediately after the sale.

  7. Prepare payment methods

    Payment must be cash or a cashier or certified check.

  8. Provide deed information

    Deed information must be provided in writing.

  9. Finalize documentation

    The county processes and records the deed after the sale.

When are McKenzie County tax sales held

The county typically conducts its tax deed sale on the third Tuesday of November each year. The exact date and details are announced by the county on its official website. As a recent example, the county scheduled a sale in mid November at 10:00 AM Central Time. Investors should always confirm details directly with the county before attending.

Maximum potential returns and expected returns on McKenzie County tax deed deals

Returns are based on the price paid and the investor’s exit plan. There is no interest paid to buyers at this auction. Profit comes from resale, rental, or owner financing after acquiring the deed. Rural land may appeal to buyers seeking long term holds or resale to recreational users. Properties closer to Watford City may offer higher demand. Conservative bidding and clear exit plans help protect returns.

Open to all investors and foreign investor participation

McKenzie County tax deed sales are open public auctions. The county requires bidders to attend in person or through an authorized representative. Payment must be made at the time of sale using approved methods. There are no residency requirements stated by the county. International investors often participate through local agents or partners. It is best to contact the Auditor and Treasurer office ahead of time to confirm requirements.

Importance of due diligence in McKenzie County tax deed investing

The county sells properties as is with no warranties. Buyers are responsible for verifying all details before bidding. Some properties may have access issues or special assessments. Federal tax liens may allow redemption after the sale. Treat the auction list as a starting point. Careful research before bidding reduces surprises and protects your capital.

What due diligence entails

  • Review parcel records and legal descriptions.
  • Confirm road access and easements.
  • Verify zoning and permitted uses.
  • Order a title search to identify liens or claims.
  • Visit the property or obtain recent photos.
  • Estimate repair or cleanup costs.
  • Set a firm maximum bid based on your exit plan.

Risks of skipping due diligence

  • Overpaying for land without legal access.
  • Unexpected costs tied to assessments or cleanup.
  • Long delays clearing title for resale.
  • Lower resale value than expected.

Buying over the counter properties in McKenzie County

McKenzie County also maintains a page for current tax foreclosure properties that may be available outside the annual auction. Availability changes and some periods may show no properties for sale. When inventory exists, buyers should contact the county to ask about purchase procedures, payment terms, and required forms. This option can be useful between auction seasons.

Why McKenzie County is a top choice for tax deed investors

McKenzie County offers large rural parcels and steady economic activity tied to energy and agriculture. The tax deed process is clearly defined. Sale dates are consistent. Minimum bid prices are published in advance. Investors who focus on access, title, and exit planning can find deals that fit long term or short term strategies.

Economic and tax advantages

  • Energy production supports local demand.
  • Major highways improve access across the county.
  • Large land inventory supports multiple investment strategies.

Real estate market overview

The real estate market varies widely by location. Properties near Watford City often see stronger demand than remote parcels. Each property should be evaluated on its own merits. Comparable sales, utility access, and local use all affect value.

Conclusion

McKenzie County, North Dakota conducts tax deed sales for county owned tax foreclosure properties. The auction is typically held on the third Tuesday of November at 10:00 AM Central Time at the county courthouse. Bidders register in person, sign required forms, and pay in full on sale day. This is a deed based auction, not an interest rate lien sale.

Investors who take time to research each parcel and plan an exit strategy are better positioned for success. Careful due diligence remains the most important step before bidding.

Pro Tips

  • Focus on legal access before anything else.
  • Match your bid to your exit strategy.
  • Confirm utility availability early.
  • Budget for title work after the sale.
  • Keep bids conservative to allow room for resale costs.

FAQs for McKenzie County tax deed buyers

Do buyers receive full ownership after purchase?

Buyers receive a county deed after processing and recording.

Should a title search still be done?

Yes. A title search helps identify issues before resale.

Can financing be used to buy at auction?

No. Full payment is required at the time of sale.

Are properties sold with occupants?

Some may be occupied. Buyers must verify occupancy.

Can buyers resell right away?

Resale timing depends on title clearance and market conditions.
